sections.heading: Matrices, Matrix Algebra & Inverses Practice Exercises

questions.q: A \( 3 \times 3 \) symmetric matrix \( Q_{k} \) has eigenvalues \( \lambda_1 = 12 \), \( \lambda_2 = 3 \), and \( \lambda_3 = 14 \). Determine the trace \( \text{tr}(Q_{k}) \).

A linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2 \) is defined by \( T(\mathbf{x}) = A\mathbf{x} \), where \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). If \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \), find \( T(\mathbf{v}) \).
questions.answer: To find \( T(\mathbf{v}) \), we multiply the matrix \( A \) by the vector \( \mathbf{v} \). \( T(\mathbf{v}) = A\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \). Performing the matrix-vector multiplication: \( T(\mathbf{v}) = \begin{pmatrix} (2 \times 1) + (1 \times 2) \\ (1 \times 1) + (3 \times 2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + 2 \\ 1 + 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \). Thus, the correct answer is \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

questions.q: Consider the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). If a point \( P=(x,y) \) is transformed by \( A \) to \( P'=(x',y') \), such that \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = A \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \), what is the image of the point \( (3,1) \) under this transformation?
questions.answer:
The transformation is defined by the matrix multiplication \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = A \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \). We are given the point \( (3,1) \), so \( \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \) and the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). Performing the matrix multiplication:

\( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (2 \times 3) + (1 \times 1) \\ (1 \times 3) + (3 \times 1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 + 1 \\ 3 + 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} \)

Therefore, the image of the point \( (3,1) \) is \( (7,6) \).

questions.q: Consider two vectors \( \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \). What is the dot product \( \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 \)?
questions.answer:
\( \text{The dot product of two vectors } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} c \\ d \end{pmatrix} \text{ is given by } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = ac + bd. \)

\( \text{In this case, } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}. \)

\( \text{Therefore, } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = (3)(-4) + (4)(3) = -12 + 12 = 0. \)

\( \text{A dot product of 0 indicates that the vectors are orthogonal.} \)

questions.q: Consider the following system of linear equations represented by the augmented matrix: \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & | & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]. Use row reduction to transform the matrix into row-echelon form and determine the unique solution \( (x, y) \) for the system. What is the value of \( x \)?
questions.answer:
We are given the augmented matrix: \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & | & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]
To transform this matrix into row-echelon form, we can perform the following row operation: \( R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 2R_1 \).
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 - 2(1) & -1 - 2(2) & | & 0 - 2(5) \end{pmatrix} \]
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & | & -10 \end{pmatrix} \]
Now, we can perform another row operation: \( R_2 \leftarrow R_2 / -5 \).
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & | & 2 \end{pmatrix} \]
This matrix is now in row-echelon form. The corresponding system of equations is:
\( x + 2y = 5 \)
\( y = 2 \)
Substitute the value of \( y \) into the first equation:
\( x + 2(2) = 5 \)
\( x + 4 = 5 \)
\( x = 1 \)
Therefore, the unique solution is \( (1, 2) \), and the value of \( x \) is 1.

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} \). Calculate the magnitude of \( \mathbf{v} \), denoted as \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert \).
questions.answer: The magnitude of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \) in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) is given by the formula \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). For the given vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} \), we have \( x=5 \) and \( y=-12 \). Therefore, \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{(5)^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \). If this vector is plotted on a standard \( xy \)-plane, it represents a directed line segment from the origin to the point \( (3,4) \). What is the geometric interpretation of the length of this vector?
choices: The vector's direction in the xy-plane.
The angle the vector makes with the positive x-axis.
The distance of the point (3,4) from the origin.
The sum of the components of the vector.
questions.answer: The length of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \) is given by its magnitude, \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). Geometrically, this corresponds to the distance from the origin \( (0,0) \) to the point \( (x,y) \) on the Cartesian plane, as described by the Pythagorean theorem. For \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \), the length is \( \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \). This value represents the distance of the point \( (3,4) \) from the origin.
